title.narrative: Croatia Disaster Preparedness and Resilience Development Policy Loan with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option (Cat DDO)

description.narrative: The Program Development Objective is to strengthen Croatia's disaster preparedness and resilience by enhancing institutional capacity at the national level and across strategic sectors, and increasing financial resilience.

The development objective of Disaster Preparedness and Resilience Development Policy Loan with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option Program is to strengthen Croatia's disaster preparedness and resilience by enhancing institutional capacity at the national level and across strategic sectors, and increasing financial resilience. Accordingly, Pillar 1—Strengthening institutional capacity for disaster preparedness and resilience, will support foundational reforms that increase the disaster preparedness of critical infrastructure and services, and that build institutional capacity for climate adaptation (CA). Pillar 2—Enhancing disaster preparedness and climate resilience in key economic sectors, will support reforms that address vulnerabilities and foster sustainable development in the energy, tourism, and housing sectors. Pillar 3—Strengthening the financial resilience of businesses and households, will advance reforms in the insurance and social protection sectors to enhance coping and recovery capacity for disaster and climate impacts. These reforms are complemented by the Cat DDO as a contingent financing mechanism that can supplement budget reserves and enhance fiscal resilience in case of major disasters. The Cat DDO supports GoC's efforts to strengthen its framework and capacity for disaster preparedness and resilience, improving public sector service and impact, and private action. Competitiveness, resilience of the economy, and better quality of life for citizens are key commitments in the GoC's program (2024–2028). Croatia has a well-established DRM framework covering all emergencies with health-related emergencies covered under the public health preparedness system. The Cat DDO leverages and complements the WBG's program in Croatia. Ongoing operations finance the upgrading of public infrastructure to meet modern building codes and safety and energy efficiency standards. The Cat DDO is consistent with the Maximizing Finance for Development (MFD) approach, being MFD-enabling and Private Capital Enabled (PCE). This operation is fully aligned with Croatia's national climate commitments and the Paris Agreement.

Share of vulnerable people receiving increased social benefit payments as a result of this reform.

comment.narrative:
Implementation is on track.
This indicator monitors enhanced benefits provided to socio-economically vulnerable and majority-women groups by measuring the share of vulnerable people receiving increased social benefit payments as a result of this reform (i.e. beneficiaries of increased GMB support). Vulnerable groups tracked by this indicator comprise eligible single-parent families, pregnant women, and survivors of domestic violence. Due to technical reasons, the Ministry was not able to provide the current data, however, according to the Ministry data from August 2025, this share was 100%.

title.narrative: The number of people with enhanced social protection benefits for stronger disaster resilience as a result of this reform.

comment.narrative:
Implementation is on track.
This indicator measures low-income populations resilience to disasters, climate shocks, and socioeconomic emergencies by tracking the number of people with enhanced social protection benefits for stronger disaster resilience as a result of this social welfare reform, i.e. all beneficiaries receiving increased guaranteed minimum benefit (GMB) support. A slight drop in the GMB recipients has been recorded due to better conditions in the market.

The number of participants in financial literacy activities reporting improved knowledge of disaster insurance products, as supported by Article 55(8) of the Insurance Act

comment.narrative:
Implementation is on track.
This indicator measures the number of participants in financial literacy activities reporting improved knowledge of disaster insurance products. Financial literacy activities related to disaster insurance products are coordinated by HANFA and funded by private insurance providers. Financial literacy activities have been implemented according to the Action Plan for Improving Consumer Financial Literacy for 2025 and 2026. Guidelines on financial literacy approved in September 2025 provide also a more structured information on the requirements for spending on financial literacy. Currently it is app. 0.03% of insurers income spent for financial literacy. HANFA continues to monitor financial literacy as per its mandate.

title.narrative: The share of registered housing associations that implement repairs and renovations, as defined by the Law on Management and Maintenance of Buildings, and reported annually

comment.narrative:
Implementation is on track.
This indicator measures the share of registered housing associations that implement repairs and renovations which will improve safety, enable energy and similar upgrades to buildings. Two Ministry programs to enable these investments (Elevators Program and Facade Program) were approved in January 2026 and the calls for proposals are expected to be published in April 2026. The total available funds are EUR 5 million; and based on demand, further investments could be planned. The call will gather information also on private (bank) contribution.

The number of prosumers using renewable energy, as reported annually and disaggregated by households and businesses

comment.narrative: Implementation is on track. This indicator measures the number of prosumers using renewable energy. The ministry continues to be very committed to promoting renewable energy and has secured funding for energy self-sufficiency for households and firms through the European Regional Development Fund in 2026 and 2027. According HEP data, as of Dec 31, 2025, 42,355 solar power plants were connected to the HEP ODS distribution network. Out of these, 34,422 solar power plants are in the household category and 7,933 solar power plants entrepreneurship category (HEP Journal, 3/2025)
